propositions: A one-time backfill script must retroactively populate complexity and clone-count time series by sampling historical commits and running metric tools.
The backfill must parse lizard output to sum cyclomatic complexity across all functions and parse jscpd JSON to extract the total clone count.
Snapshots written during backfill must be timestamped with the commit's date (via git show format=%cI), not the wall-clock backfill execution time, to preserve historical trends.
If either metric tool is absent or errors during a commit measurement, that commit must be skipped and logged without aborting the backfill run.
All backfilled snapshots must carry metadata tags source=snapshot and confidence=high, and be written through the same write_snapshot interface as the going-forward path.

The test suite (scripts tier, with measure_tree stubbed) must validate that sampled commits produce correctly-typed snapshots, that failed measurements are skipped gracefully, and that snapshot timestamps equal commit dates.
